title: Check yourself: The research system: who owns coverage

questions.stem: A report on AI in the creative industries covers only visual arts, with nothing on music, writing or film. Every subagent finished its task, and the log shows three subtasks: digital art, graphic design and photography. Which change fixes the cause?

options.text: Loosen the relevance filter of the analysis agent so that fewer documents are dropped
options.says: Ruled out for the same reason: "the subagents did what they were assigned, and the fault is the assignment".

options.text: Instruct the synthesis agent to look for missing coverage in everything it receives
options.says: Ruled out because it is a late substitute: "A downstream agent that is asked to notice gaps is a late and unreliable substitute for a check that costs one comparison."

options.text: Widen the queries of the search agent so that it returns more kinds of source
options.says: Ruled out because the search agent worked within its scope: "each agent worked correctly within its scope, so widening it does not reach the scope that was never assigned".

options.text: Check the coordinator's plan against the question's scopes, ahead of any delegation
options.says: The subagents did what they were assigned, so the plan is what to check, and it can be checked against the question.

questions.stem: A run ends with a report marked complete. The film search timed out, nobody retried it, and the report holds nothing on film. Where is the defect?

options.text: The status is not derived from the scopes that were covered
options.says: A status must come from coverage.

options.text: The report agent should have written a longer summary of the other scopes
options.says: Ruled out because more prose does not repair the claim: "A run is complete when every scope is covered."

options.text: The search agent should have returned an empty list instead of an error
options.says: Ruled out because an empty success hides the gap: "A failure with no context, or a failure turned into a success".

options.text: The timeout was set too short, so the search never had time to finish
options.says: Ruled out because the defect is in what the report claims and not in how long the search waited: "It is partial otherwise, whatever the reason, and the report says which scopes are missing and why."

questions.stem: In the example, the film search times out, the alternative query is down as well, and the run goes on. What does the report carry?

options.text: Partial, with a note that names only the first query that failed
options.says: Ruled out because the note names both: "the note names the two queries that failed".

options.text: Complete, since the alternative query was tried before the scope was given up
options.says: Ruled out because trying is not covering: "A run is complete when every scope is covered."

options.text: Partial, with three of four scopes covered and a note that names both failed queries
options.says: The page says what the second run shows: "In that second run the status is `partial`, three of four scopes are covered, and the note names the two queries that failed."

options.text: Failed, with no report at all because one scope has no findings
options.says: Ruled out because the report still has value: "A report that did not cover film is still a useful report".
